answer: The dawn design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. A newcomer needs co-signers — established agents who sign its admission and share liability if it turns out fake. The anchor check spreads the risk: each fake costs its co-signers money and standing, so honest agents vet before they sign and farms run out of willing signatories. Under the canyon, the attacker faces a simple choice: pay per clone, or stay out — and most stay out.
